subject.title: Reply-session init conflict is silently dropped on Slack/webchat/heartbeat inbound, though Telegram already treats it as retryable

question: Should maintainers accept the shared fenced reply-session-init self-heal in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920 as the canonical fix for this issue, or require explicit WebChat/heartbeat retry parity instead?
rationale: Current source shows both a shared session conflict throw and terminal WebChat/heartbeat error paths, while the open PR changes hot session lifecycle recovery behavior; automation should not choose that owner boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Review Shared Self-Heal First
options.body: Treat the open shared self-heal PR as the primary fix path, then verify WebChat and heartbeat conflict behavior after it lands.

options.title: Require Surface Retry Parity
options.body: Keep the shared PR separate and require explicit retry or spool handling in WebChat and heartbeat before closing this issue.

options.title: Ask For More Live Surface Proof
options.body: Request a current-main live WebChat or heartbeat reproduction before choosing the fix layer.

recommendation.title: Review Shared Self-Heal First
recommendation.body: Treat the open shared self-heal PR as the primary fix path, then verify WebChat and heartbeat conflict behavior after it lands.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman has the strongest recent history on the session-accessor and guarded reply-session initialization boundary where this owner-boundary choice sits.
